dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about these attention issues and when you first noticed a change in her behavior?

My mom is the one who thinks I have an attention problem, but I just don't care about school anymore. Since I started high school, everything feels different and I'd rather just be by myself than go to cheer practice.
I see. Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or your sleep patterns since these feelings started?
No, I sleep the same as always and I'm not especially tired. I just don't feel like doing anything, and it's annoying that my mom keeps making a big deal out of it.

It's understandable that you feel frustrated when others don't seem to get where you're coming from. Have you been feeling particularly sad, empty, or hopeless lately, or is it mostly just a lack of interest in things you used to enjoy?

I wouldn't say I'm hopeless, I just feel unhappy with how things are at school and with my friends right now. I don't really want to hang out with the cheer team anymore, and I'd honestly just rather be left alone.

Thank you for being open with me. Your mother mentioned concerns about your attention—do you find it difficult to focus on things even when they do interest you, or does it just feel like your mind is elsewhere lately?

I can focus fine if I actually care about what's happening, but most of the time my mind is just on how much I hate my current social situation. It isn't that I can't pay attention; I just don't have any motivation to put effort into school right now.
I appreciate you clarifying that for me. Aside from feeling unhappy and wanting to be alone, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or has your weight changed significantly recently?
My weight and appetite are exactly the same as they've always been. I don't have any problems with eating; I'm just not in the mood to be around people.

You mentioned being unhappy with your social situation; did something specific happen with your friends recently? Also, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself?

RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS
I'm glad to hear the thyroid results are normal. Could you tell me more about what's been happening with your friends, and have you had any thoughts of self-harm or hurting yourself
I’ve never thought about hurting myself or anyone else, and I'm definitely not suicidal. Things are just weird with my friends since high school started, and I’m just over the whole social scene.
I'm glad to hear you're safe. Have you been feeling more irritable or quick to anger lately, and did you ever have similar feelings before starting high school?
I definitely get annoyed a lot faster now, especially when my mom won't stop bugging me about my grades. I never felt this way before high school; everything was fine until this year started.
It sounds like the transition to high school has been quite stressful for you. Do you often feel guilty about things or feel like you're not good enough, and have you been using any alcohol

I don't drink or do any of that stuff, so you don't have to worry about that. I wouldn't say I feel guilty, just really frustrated that everything changed and I'm not happy with my life right now. I don't feel "not good enough," I just feel like I'm done trying to fit in with everyone.
It's clear that the social shift has had a big impact on you. Do you ever feel nervous or anxious about interacting with your peers, or have you noticed any physical issues
I don't really get nervous or have any physical problems like shaking or anything. It's more that I just find everyone annoying and I'd honestly just rather stay in my room than deal with them.

Does your mood stay low most of the day, every day, or does it tend to shift if something good happens? Also, is there any history of depression or similar issues in your family?

How have your grades changed since starting high school, and do you feel like you're falling behind because you can't focus or because you simply don't want to do the work?
My grades have definitely dropped, but it's not because I'm lost or can't understand the material. I just don't have the motivation to do the work when everything else feels so miserable.

Since you mentioned your mother is concerned about your attention, I'd like to know if there have been any other major life changes lately besides starting high school. Also, does anyone in your family have a history of depression, anxiety, or other behavioral health issues?

There haven't been any other big changes, just high school starting and everything feeling different. As far as I know, my family doesn't have any history of that kind of stuff. I'm just tired of my mom thinking there's something wrong with my brain when I'm just unhappy.
When your mind is "elsewhere" during class, are you usually stuck thinking about these social frustrations, or is it more like your mind just goes blank? I'd also like to

I'm usually just thinking about how much I don't want to be there or dwelling on the drama with my friends. My mind doesn't go blank; I’m just focused on how unhappy I am instead of what the teacher is saying.

It sounds like your attention issues are tied directly to your mood and the stress of your new environment. Since these feelings started, have you had any trouble with teachers or followed through on any

I haven't had any trouble with my teachers, and I still follow the rules and do what I'm told when I have to. I'm not acting out or getting into fights; I'm just quiet and don't participate because I don't see the point.
Since this began exactly when high school started, how many months has it been? Have you ever had a time where you felt extremely high energy, like you didn't need sleep at all?
It's been about three or four months since school started and this all began. And no, I've never had that kind of high energy; if anything, I just feel more drained from being annoyed all the time.

It sounds like your symptoms are a direct reaction to the stress and social changes of starting high school rather than a chronic condition. I have enough information to form a conclusion.
